description: Read rows from one or more Notion tables. Each query names the table by data_source_id (what notion-search_pages-1 returns for a "data_source" result) or by database_id, and may carry a Notion filter, sorts, and a cursor. Notion has no batch query endpoint, so the queries run as bounded concurrent single requests under the connection limit of about three per second: one round trip per query, so keep the batch small. Each query answers on its own — one failure returns an error for that query and rows for the rest. Every row keeps its raw Notion properties alongside the extracted title, and its own next_cursor; send that cursor back on the same table to read the next page.

queries.description: The tables to read, one provider call each.

data_source_id.description: The table to read. Preferred: it costs one request instead of two.

database_id.description: The database holding the table, when the data source id is unknown. Its first data source is read.

filter.description: A Notion filter object, forwarded untouched. See Notion's filter reference.

cursor.description: The cursor this table returned last time. Paging is per table, because each table is its own provider call with its own pages.

data_source_id.description: The table that actually answered, so a caller that passed a database_id sees which data source was read.

properties.description: The row's raw Notion property values, unflattened.

query.description: Lenient ingress on POST /v1/data_sources/{data_source_id}/query. Property values stay open: Notion's property union grows every year and a stale copy would reject rows Notion serves.

database.description: Lenient ingress on GET /v1/databases/{database_id}, used only to turn a database_id into the data source to read.

quirks.endpoint: POST /v1/data_sources/{data_source_id}/query, and GET /v1/databases/{database_id} first when the caller gave a database_id.
quirks.why_execute: Notion has no batch query endpoint, so the plural contract runs as a fan-out with per-item results and a cursor per table. A query given a database_id also needs a lookup call before it. A declarative http mapping expresses neither.
quirks.data_source_split: Since API version 2025-09-03 a database is a container of one or more data sources, and POST /v1/databases/{id}/query is gone. This node calls POST /v1/data_sources/{id}/query.
quirks.first_data_source_wins: A database_id with several data sources has no single right answer, so the first one is read. The answer names the data_source_id it used, so the choice is never silent.
quirks.filter_grammar: Notion's filter and sort grammars are deep recursive unions that grow with every property type. They are forwarded untouched rather than remodelled, so a stale copy cannot reject a filter Notion accepts.
quirks.truncated_property_arrays: Notion truncates paginated property arrays (title, rich_text, people, relation) to 25 items inside a row. Read the rest with the page property endpoint.
quirks.result_cap: One query walks at most 10,000 rows through its cursors.
